name: Butylated hydroxytoluene
aliases: E321, BHT, butylated hydroxytoluene, hidroxitolueno butilado, 2,6-di-tert-butyl-p-cresol
what_is: A synthetic antioxidant used to preserve the freshness and extend the shelf-life of food fats and oils.
why_botia: BHT is E321, an authorised antioxidant — but it is not BHA. EFSA reviewed it separately in 2012 and set an intake limit of 0.25 mg/kg body weight a day. IARC puts BHT in Group 3: not classifiable as carcinogenic to humans.
can_1: Spot E321 or BHT in the ingredient list.
can_2: Show BHT's own EFSA intake limit and its IARC Group 3 classification.
cannot_1: Determine if the BHT has migrated from the packaging material or was added directly to the food.
